title: Aparokṣānubhūti
subtitle: Direct experience of the Self

source.edition: Sanskrit text and word-meaning collation; Swami Vimuktananda's Belur Math edition (1938) noted by the source
source.digitalText: Sanskrit text and lexical entries cross-checked against Shlokam
source.crossCheck: Traditional attribution to Ādi Śaṅkara; closing colophon included

translationCredit: Original English translation; concise lexical glosses normalized for this reader.

units.label: Verse 1
units.deva:
श्रीहरिं परमानन्दमुपदेष्टारमीश्वरम्।
व्यापकं सर्वलोकानां कारणं तं नमाम्यहम्।।1।।
units.translation: I bow to Śrī Hari, supreme bliss and primordial teacher, the Lord who pervades all worlds and is their cause.

units.label: Verse 2
units.deva:
अपरोक्षानुभूतिर्वै प्रोच्यते मोक्षसिद्धये।
सद्भिरेषा प्रयत्नेन वीक्षणीया मुहुर्मुहुः।।2।।
units.translation: This direct knowledge is taught for liberation; the clear-hearted should examine it, steadily and with effort.

units.label: Verse 3
units.deva:
स्ववर्णाश्रमधर्मेण तपसा हरितोषणात्।
साधनं प्रभवेत्पुंसां वैराग्यादिचतुष्टयम्।।3।।
units.translation: Austerity, fulfilment of one's duties, and worship of Hari give rise to the four qualifications beginning with dispassion.

gloss.en: by one's caste and stage duties

units.label: Verse 4
units.deva:
ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तेषु वैराग्यं विषयेष्वनु।
यथैव काकविष्ठायां वैराग्यं तद्धि निर्मलम्।।4।।
units.translation: Pure dispassion regards every object—from Brahmā down to the immovable—as worthless as a crow's droppings.

units.label: Verse 5
units.deva:
नित्यमात्मस्वरूपं हि दृश्यं तद्विपरीतगम्।
एवं यो निश्चयः सम्यग्विवेको वस्तुनः स वै।।5।।
units.translation: The Self alone is permanent; whatever is seen is its opposite. Firm discernment of this is true discrimination.

units.label: Verse 6
units.deva:
सदैव वासनात्यागः शमोऽयमिति शब्दितः।
निग्रहो बाह्यवृत्तीनां दम इत्यभिधीयते।।6।।
units.translation: Letting go of latent desires is called śama; restraining the outward activity of the senses is called dama.

units.label: Verse 7
units.deva:
विषयेभ्यः परावृत्तिः परमोपरतिर्हि सा।
सहनं सर्वदुःखानां तितिक्षा सा शुभा मता।।7।।
units.translation: Turning entirely from sense objects is uparati; patient endurance of all suffering is the auspicious titikṣā.

units.label: Verse 8
units.deva:
निगमाचार्यवाक्येषु भक्तिः श्रद्धेति विश्रुता।
चित्तैकाग्र्यं तु सल्लक्ष्ये समाधानमिति स्मृतम्।।8।।
units.translation: Faith in the Veda and teacher's words is śraddhā; fixing the mind on Being is samādhāna.

units.label: Verse 9
units.deva:
संसारबन्धनिर्मुक्तिः कथं स्यान्मे दयानिधे।
इति या सुदृढा बुद्धिर्वक्तव्या सा मुमुक्षुता।।9।।
units.translation: “When shall I be freed from worldly bondage, O compassionate Lord?” This firm longing is mumukṣutā.

units.label: Verse 10
units.deva:
उक्तसाधनयुक्तेन विचारः पुरुषेण हि।
कर्तव्यो ज्ञानसिद्ध्यर्थमात्मनः शुभमिच्छता।।10।।
units.translation: One seeking one's own good, furnished with those qualifications, should inquire in order to attain knowledge.

units.label: Verse 11
units.deva:
नोत्पद्यते विना ज्ञानं विचारेणान्यसाधनैः।
यथा पदार्थभानं हि प्रकाशेन विना क्वचित्।।11।।
units.translation: Knowledge arises through inquiry alone, as objects are never perceived without light.

units.label: Verse 12
units.deva:
कोऽहं कथमिदं जातं को वा कर्तास्य विद्यते।
उपादानं किमस्तीह विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।12।।
units.translation: “Who am I? How did this arise? Who is its maker? What is its material cause?” Such is inquiry.

units.label: Verse 13
units.deva:
नाहं भूतगणो देहो नाहं चाक्षगणस्तथा।
एतद्विलक्षणः कश्चिद्विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।13।।
units.translation: I am neither the body composed of elements nor the group of senses; inquiry recognizes me as distinct from them.

units.label: Verse 14
units.deva:
अज्ञानप्रभवं सर्वं ज्ञानेन प्रविलीयते।
संकल्पो विविधः कर्ता विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।14।।
units.translation: All that ignorance produces is dissolved by knowledge; thought itself is the maker of this varied world—this is inquiry.

units.label: Verse 15
units.deva:
एतयोर्यदुपादानमेकं सूक्ष्मं सदव्ययम्।
यथैव मृद्धटादीनां विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।15।।
units.translation: The subtle, single, changeless Being is the material cause of both ignorance and thought, as clay is of pots.

units.label: Verse 16
units.deva:
अहमेकोऽपि सूक्ष्मश्च ज्ञाता साक्षी सदव्ययः।
तदहं नात्र संदेहो विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।16।।
units.translation: I am the one subtle knower and changeless witness; there is no doubt that I am That.

units.label: Verse 17
units.deva:
आत्मा विनिष्कलो ह्येको देहो बहुभिरावृतः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।17।।
units.translation: The Self is one and partless, the body many-parted; to see them as identical—what could be greater ignorance?

units.label: Verse 18
units.deva:
आत्मा नियामकश्चान्तर्देहो नियम्यबाह्यकः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।18।।
units.translation: The Self rules within; the body is ruled and external. To identify the two—what greater ignorance?

units.label: Verse 19
units.deva:
आत्मा ज्ञानमयः पुण्यो देहो मांसमयोऽशुचिः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।19।।
units.translation: The Self is consciousness and pure; the body is flesh and impure. To equate them—what greater ignorance?

units.label: Verse 20
units.deva:
आत्मा प्रकाशकः स्वच्छो देहस्तामस उच्यते।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।20।।
units.translation: The Self illumines and is clear; the body is inert and dark. To call them one—what greater ignorance?

units.label: Verse 21
units.deva:
आत्मा नित्यो हि सद्रूपो देहोऽनित्यो ह्यसन्मयः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।21।।
units.translation: The Self is eternal Being, the body transient and unreal. To confuse them—what greater ignorance?

units.label: Verse 22
units.deva:
आत्मनस्तत्प्रकाशत्वं यत्पदार्थावभासनम्।
नाग्न्यादिदीप्तिवद्दीप्तिर्भवत्यान्ध्यं यतो निशि।।22।।
units.translation: The Self shines by making all objects manifest; its light is unlike fire, whose radiance leaves darkness elsewhere.

gloss.en: like the light of fire etc.

units.label: Verse 23
units.deva:
देहोऽहमित्ययं मूढो मत्वा तिष्ठत्यहो जनः।
ममायमित्यपि ज्ञात्वा घटद्रष्टेव सर्वदा।।23।।
units.translation: How strange: the fool says “I am the body” while calling the body “mine,” as one who sees a pot knows it apart from himself.

units.label: Verse 24
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैवाहं समः शान्तः सच्चिदानन्दलक्षणः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।24।।
units.translation: “I am Brahman, tranquil and even, whose nature is Being, Consciousness, and Bliss; I am not the unreal body”—the wise call this knowledge.

gloss.en: of the nature of Existence, Knowledge, and Bliss

units.label: Verse 25
units.deva:
निर्विकारो निराकारो निरवद्योऽहमव्ययः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।25।।
units.translation: I am changeless, formless, faultless, and imperishable; the body is unreal and I am not that. This is knowledge.

units.label: Verse 26
units.deva:
निरामयो निराभासो निर्विकल्पोऽहमाततः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।26।।
units.translation: I am free of illness, beyond appearance and distinctions, all-pervading; I am not the unreal body. This is knowledge.

units.label: Verse 27
units.deva:
निर्गुणो निष्क्रियो नित्यो नित्यमुक्तोऽहमच्युतः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।27।।
units.translation: I am without qualities or action, eternal, ever free, and unfailing; I am not the unreal body. This is knowledge.

units.label: Verse 28
units.deva:
निर्मलो निश्चलोऽनन्तः शुद्धोऽहमजरोऽमरः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।28।।
units.translation: I am stainless, still, limitless, pure, ageless, and deathless; the unreal body is not I. This is knowledge.

units.label: Verse 29
units.deva:
स्वदेहं शोभनं त्यक्त्वा पुरुषाख्यं च संमतम्।
किं मूर्ख शून्यमात्मानं देहातीतं करोषि भो।।29।।
units.translation: Fool, why do you call the Self—a blissful, existent reality within and distinct from your body—utterly nonexistent, though it is known as Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 30
units.deva:
स्वात्मानं श्रृणु मूर्ख त्वं श्रुत्या युक्त्या च पूरुषम्।
देहातीतं सदाकारं सुदुर्दर्शं भवादृशाम्।।30।।
units.translation: Fool, learn through scripture and reasoning the Puruṣa that is your own Self, beyond the body, pure Being, hard for one like you to discern.

units.label: Verse 31
units.deva:
अहंशब्देन विख्यात एक एव स्थितः परः।
स्थूलत्वान्नैकतां प्राप्तः कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।31।।
units.translation: The supreme Puruṣa, called “I,” is one; gross bodies are many. How could this body be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 32
units.deva:
अहं द्रष्टृतया सिद्धो देहो दृश्यतया स्थितः।
ममायमिति निर्देशात्कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।32।।
units.translation: “I” is the subject that knows; the body is seen as “mine.” How, then, could the body be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 33
units.deva:
अहं विकारहीनस्तु देहो नित्यं विकारवान्।
इति प्रतीयते साक्षात्कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।33।।
units.translation: Directly, the “I” is changeless and the body constantly changes. How could the body be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 34
units.deva:
यस्मात्परमिति श्रुत्या तया पुरुषलक्षणम्।
विनिर्णीतं विशुद्धेन कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।34।।
units.translation: The pure scriptures determine Puruṣa to be higher than all else. How could the body be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 35
units.deva:
सर्वं पुरुष एवेति सूक्ते पुरुषसंज्ञिते।
अप्युच्यते यतः श्रुत्या कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।35।।
units.translation: Scripture in the Puruṣa Sūkta declares that all this is Puruṣa. How could this body alone be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 36
units.deva:
असङ्गः पुरुषः प्रोक्तो बृहदारण्यकेऽपि च।
अनन्तमलसंसृष्टः कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।36।।
units.translation: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka also calls Puruṣa unattached. How could this body, bound up with countless impurities, be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 37
units.deva:
तत्रैव च समाख्यातः स्वयंज्योतिर्हि पूरुषः।
जडः परप्रकाश्योऽयं कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।37।।
units.translation: There Puruṣa is said to be self-luminous. How could this inert body, lit by another, be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 38
units.deva:
प्रोक्तोऽपि कर्मकाण्डेन ह्यात्मा देहाद्विलक्षणः।
नित्यश्च तत्फलं भुङ्क्ते देहपातादनन्तरम्।।38।।
units.translation: The ritual portion too teaches that the Self differs from the body and endures beyond its fall, receiving the fruits of action.

gloss.en: after the fall of the body

units.label: Verse 39
units.deva:
लिङ्गं चानेकसंयुक्तं चलं दृश्यं विकारि च।
अव्यापकमसद्रूपं तत्कथं स्यात्पुमानयम्।।39।।
units.translation: The subtle body is composite, moving, visible, changeful, limited, and unreal. How could it be Puruṣa?

units.label: Verse 40
units.deva:
एवं देहद्वयादन्य आत्मा पुरुष ईश्वरः।
सर्वात्मा सर्वरूपश्च सर्वातीतोऽहमव्ययः।।40।।
units.translation: Thus, beyond both bodies, the immutable Self is the Lord and Puruṣa: the Self of all, taking every form yet beyond all.

units.label: Verse 41
units.deva:
इत्यात्मदेहभानेन प्रपञ्चस्यैव सत्यता।
यथोक्ता तर्कशास्त्रेण ततः किं पुरुषार्थता।।41।।
units.translation: This distinction between Self and body can establish the world's apparent reality by logic; but what human end does that serve?

gloss.en: by the distinction of self and body

units.label: Verse 42
units.deva:
इत्यात्मदेहभेदेन देहात्मत्वं निवारितम्।
इदानीं देहभेदस्य ह्यसत्त्वं स्फुटमुच्यते।।42।।
units.translation: The claim that the body is the Self is refuted by distinguishing them; now the body's separateness will be shown unreal.

gloss.en: by the distinction of self and body
of the difference of the body

units.label: Verse 43
units.deva:
चैतन्यस्यैकरूपत्वाद्भेदो युक्तो न कर्हिचित्।
जीवत्वं च मृषा ज्ञेयं रज्ज्वां सर्पग्रहो यथा।।43।।
units.translation: Consciousness is one, so real division cannot occur; individuality is as false as seeing a snake in a rope.

units.label: Verse 44
units.deva:
रज्ज्वज्ञानात्क्षणेनैव यद्वद्रज्जुर्हि सर्पिणी।
भाति तद्वच्चितिः साक्षाद्विश्वाकारेण केवला।।44।।
units.translation: Just as an unknown rope seems to become a snake, pure awareness seems to be the entire universe.

gloss.en: in the form of the universe

units.label: Verse 45
units.deva:
उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य ब्रह्मणोऽन्यन्न विद्यते।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रपञ्चोऽयं ब्रह्मैवास्ति न चेतरत्।।45।।
units.translation: Nothing other than Brahman is the material cause of the universe; therefore all this is Brahman alone.

units.label: Verse 46
units.deva:
व्याप्यव्यापकता मिथ्या सर्वमात्मेति शासनात्।
इति ज्ञाते परे तत्त्वे भेदस्यावसरः कुतः।।46।।
units.translation: If all is Self, the notions of pervader and pervaded are false. Once the highest truth is known, where can difference remain?

units.label: Verse 47
units.deva:
श्रुत्या निवारितं नूनं नानात्वं स्वमुखेन हि।
कथं भासो भवेदन्यः स्थिते चाद्वयकारणे।।47।।
units.translation: Scripture directly denies plurality; when the nondual cause is established, how could the world be other than it?

units.label: Verse 48
units.deva:
दोषोऽपि विहितः श्रुत्या मृत्योर्मृत्युं स गच्छति।
इह पश्यति नानात्वं मायया वञ्चितो नरः।।48।।
units.translation: Scripture warns that one deceived by māyā who sees multiplicity goes from death to death.

units.label: Verse 49
units.deva:
ब्रह्मणः सर्वभूतानि जायन्ते परमात्मनः।
तस्मादेतानि ब्रह्मैव भवन्तीत्यवधारयेत्।।49।।
units.translation: All beings arise from supreme Brahman; know them therefore as Brahman itself.

units.label: Verse 50
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैव सर्वनामानि रूपाणि विविधानि च।
कर्माण्यपि समग्राणि बिभर्तीति श्रुतिर्जगौ।।50।।
units.translation: Scripture says Brahman bears every name, varied form, and all action.

units.label: Verse 51
units.deva:
सुवर्णाज्जायमानस्य सुवर्णत्वं च शाश्वतम्।
ब्रह्मणो जायमानस्य ब्रह्मत्वं च तथा भवेत्।।51।।
units.translation: As objects made of gold remain gold, beings arising from Brahman remain Brahman.

units.label: Verse 52
units.deva:
स्वल्पमप्यन्तरं कृत्वा जीवात्मपरमात्मनोः।
योऽवतिष्ठति मूढात्मा भयं तस्याभिभाषितम्।।52।।
units.translation: Fear belongs to the deluded one who maintains even the slightest division between individual Self and supreme Self.

units.label: Verse 53
units.deva:
यत्राज्ञानाद्भवेद्द्वैतमितरस्तत्र पश्यति।
आत्मत्वेन यदा सर्वं नेतरस्तत्र चाण्वपि।।53।।
units.translation: Under ignorance one sees another; when all is known as Self, no other appears, even in the smallest degree.

units.label: Verse 54
units.deva:
यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतानि ह्यात्मत्वेन विजानतः।
न वै तस्य भवेन्मोहो न च शोकोऽद्वितीयतः।।54।।
units.translation: For one who knows all beings as Self, there is no delusion or grief, for there is no second.

units.label: Verse 55
units.deva:
अयमात्मा हि ब्रह्मैव सर्वात्मकतया स्थितः।
इति निर्धारितं श्रुत्या बृहदारण्यसंस्थया।।55।।
units.translation: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka declares that this Self, which is the Self of all, is Brahman.

units.label: Verse 56
units.deva:
अनुभूतोऽप्ययं लोको व्यवहारक्षमोऽपि सन्।
असद्रूपो यथा स्वप्न उत्तरक्षणबाधतः।।56।।
units.translation: Though experienced and useful in daily dealings, this world is unreal like a dream, contradicted when the next moment comes.

units.label: Verse 57
units.deva:
स्वप्नो जागरणेऽलीकः स्वप्नेऽपि न हि जागरः।
द्वयमेव लये नास्ति लयोऽपि ह्युभयोर्न च।।57।।
units.translation: Dream vanishes in waking and waking is absent in dream; in deep sleep both are absent, and sleep itself is not present in either.

units.label: Verse 58
units.deva:
त्रयमेवं भवेन्मिथ्या गुणत्रयविनिर्मितम्।
अस्य द्रष्टा गुणातीतो नित्यो ह्येकश्चिदात्मकः।।58।।
units.translation: The three states, shaped by the three guṇas, are unreal; their witness is eternal, one, and consciousness itself, beyond the guṇas.

units.label: Verse 59
units.deva:
यद्वन्मृदि घटभ्रान्तिं शुक्तौ वा रजतस्थितिम्।
तद्वद्ब्रह्मणि जीवत्वं भ्रान्त्या पश्यति न स्वतः।।59।।
units.translation: As jar in earth or silver in shell vanishes when its basis is known, so the jīva is not seen apart from Brahman.

units.label: Verse 60
units.deva:
यथा मृदि घटो नाम कनके कुण्डलाभिधा।
शुक्तौ हि रजतख्यातिर्जीवशब्दस्तथा परे।।60।।
units.translation: Earth is called jar, gold earring, and shell silver; likewise Brahman is called jīva.

units.label: Verse 61
units.deva:
यथैव व्योम्नि नीलत्वं यथा नीरं मरुस्थले।
पुरुषत्वं यथा स्थाणौ तद्वद्विश्वं चिदात्मनि।।61।।
units.translation: As blue in the sky, water in a mirage, and a person in a post are illusory, so the world appears in consciousness.

units.label: Verse 62
units.deva:
यथैव शून्ये वेतालो गन्धर्वाणां पुरं यथा।
यथाकाशे द्विचन्द्रत्वं तद्वत्सत्ये जगत्स्थितिः।।62।।
units.translation: As a ghost in a void, a city in the sky, or a second moon are imagined, so the universe appears in the Real.

units.label: Verse 63
units.deva:
यथा तरङ्गकल्लोलैर्जलमेव स्फुरत्यलम्।
पात्ररूपेण ताम्रं हि ब्रह्माण्डौघैस्तथात्मता।।63।।
units.translation: Water alone appears as waves and copper as vessels; similarly the Self appears as the whole universe.

units.label: Verse 64
units.deva:
घटनाम्ना यथा पृथ्वी पटनाम्ना हि तन्तवः।
जगन्नाम्ना चिदाभाति ज्ञेयं तत्तदभावतः।।64।।
units.translation: Earth is called jar and threads cloth; consciousness appears as the world. Know it by negating these names.

units.label: Verse 65
units.deva:
सर्वोऽपि व्यवहारस्तु ब्रह्मणा क्रियते जनैः।
अज्ञानान्न विजानन्ति मृदेव हि घटादिकम्।।65।।
units.translation: People act through Brahman without knowing it, as they fail to see that pots are only clay.

units.label: Verse 66
units.deva:
कार्यकारणता नित्यमास्ते घटमृदोर्यथा।
तथैव श्रुतियुक्तिभ्यां प्रपञ्चब्रह्मणोरिह।।66।।
units.translation: As jar and clay remain linked as effect and cause, scripture and reason show the world and Brahman similarly related.

units.label: Verse 67
units.deva:
गृह्यमाणे घटे यद्वन्मृत्तिका भाति वै बलात्।
वीक्ष्यमाणे प्रपञ्चेऽपि ब्रह्मैवाभाति भासुरम्।।67।।
units.translation: Clay is evident when one grasps a pot; Brahman, radiant, is evident when one examines the world.

units.label: Verse 68
units.deva:
सदैवात्मा विशुद्धोऽपि ह्यशुद्धो भाति वै सदा।
यथैव द्विविधा रज्जुर्ज्ञानिनोऽज्ञानिनोऽनिशम्।।68।।
units.translation: Though ever pure, the Self seems impure to the ignorant, just as the same rope is seen differently by knower and fool.

units.label: Verse 69
units.deva:
यथैव मृन्मयः कुम्भस्तद्वद्देहोऽपि चिन्मयः।
आत्मानात्मविभागोऽयं मुधैव क्रियते बुधैः।।69।।
units.translation: As a jar is only clay, the body too is consciousness; the wise see the Self/non-Self division as baseless.

units.label: Verse 70
units.deva:
सर्पत्वेन यथा रज्जू रजतत्वेन शुक्तिका।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।70।।
units.translation: As a rope is mistaken for a snake and shell for silver, the ignorant decide the Self is the body.

units.label: Verse 71
units.deva:
घटत्वेन यथा पृथ्वी पटत्वेनैव तन्तवः।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।71।।
units.translation: As earth is called a jar and threads a cloth, so the deluded mistake the Self for the body.

units.label: Verse 72
units.deva:
कनकं कुण्डलत्वेन तरङ्गत्वेन वै जलम्।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।72।।
units.translation: As gold is called an earring and water a wave, so the deluded mistake the Self for the body.

units.label: Verse 73
units.deva:
पुरुषत्वेन वै स्थाणुर्जलत्वेन मरीचिका।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।73।।
units.translation: As a stump is mistaken for a man and a mirage for water, so the deluded mistake the Self for the body.

units.label: Verse 74
units.deva:
गृहत्वेनैव काष्ठानि खङ्गत्वेनैव लोहता।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।74।।
units.translation: As timber is named a house and iron a sword, so the deluded mistake the Self for the body.

units.label: Verse 75
units.deva:
यथा वृक्षविपर्यासो जलाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।75।।
units.translation: As water can make a tree seem reflected, ignorance makes the Self appear embodied.

units.label: Verse 76
units.deva:
पोतेन गच्छतः पुंसः सर्वं भातीव चञ्चलम्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।76।।
units.translation: To a passenger in a boat, everything seems to move; likewise ignorance makes the Self appear embodied.

units.label: Verse 77
units.deva:
पीतत्वं हि यथा शुभ्रे दोषाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।77।।
units.translation: As a defect makes white appear yellow, ignorance makes the Self seem to be the body.

units.label: Verse 78
units.deva:
चक्षुर्भ्यां भ्रमशीलाभ्यां सर्वं भाति भ्रमात्मकम्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।78।।
units.translation: As blurred eyes make everything seem blurred, ignorance makes the Self appear embodied.

units.label: Verse 79
units.deva:
अलातं भ्रमणेनैव वर्तुलं भाति सूर्यवत्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।79।।
units.translation: A spinning firebrand seems to draw a circle; likewise ignorance makes the Self seem to be the body.

units.label: Verse 80
units.deva:
महत्त्वे सर्ववस्तूनामणुत्वं ह्यतिदूरतः।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।80।।
units.translation: Great things seem tiny from afar; likewise ignorance makes the Self appear embodied.

units.label: Verse 81
units.deva:
सूक्ष्मत्वे सर्ववस्तूनां स्थूलत्वं चोपनेत्रतः।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।81।।
units.translation: Through a lens, tiny things seem large; likewise ignorance makes the Self seem embodied.

units.label: Verse 82
units.deva:
काचभूमौ जलत्वं वा जलभूमौ हि काचता।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।82।।
units.translation: Glass may look like water and water like glass; likewise ignorance makes the Self seem embodied.

units.label: Verse 83
units.deva:
यद्वदग्नौ मणित्वं हि मणौ वा वह्निता पुमान्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।83।।
units.translation: A gem may seem like fire, and fire like a gem; likewise ignorance makes the Self seem embodied.

units.label: Verse 84
units.deva:
अभ्रेषु सत्सु धावत्सु धावन्निव यथा शशी।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।84।।
units.translation: Moving clouds make the moon seem to move; likewise ignorance makes the Self seem embodied.

units.label: Verse 85
units.deva:
यथैव दिग्विपर्यासो मोहाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।85।।
units.translation: Confusion reverses the directions; ignorance likewise produces the mistaken sense that the Self is a body.

units.label: Verse 86
units.deva:
यथा शशी जले भाति चञ्चलत्वेन कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।86।।
units.translation: The moon reflected in water seems unsteady; likewise ignorance makes the Self seem embodied.

units.label: Verse 87
units.deva:
एवमात्मनि नज्ञाते देहाध्यासो हि जायते।
स एवात्मा परिज्ञातो लीयते च परात्मनि।।87।।
units.translation: When the Self is unknown, body-identification arises; when the Self is known, that error dissolves into the supreme Self.

units.label: Verse 88
units.deva:
सर्वमात्मतया ज्ञातं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
अभावात्सर्वभावानां देहानां चात्मता कुतः।।88।।
units.translation: If the whole movable and immovable world is known as Self, where could bodies possess a separate self?

units.label: Verse 89
units.deva:
आत्मानं सततं जानन्कालं नय महामते।
प्रारब्धमखिलं भुञ्जन्नोद्वेगं कर्तुमर्हसि।।89।।
units.translation: Great-minded one, contemplate the Self continually while experiencing the results already in motion; do not be distressed.

units.label: Verse 90
units.deva:
उत्पन्नेऽप्यात्मविज्ञाने प्रारब्धं नैव मुञ्चति।
इति यच्छ्रूयते शास्त्रात्तन्निराक्रियतेऽधुना।।90।।
units.translation: The claim that past action persists after Self-knowledge is now refuted.

units.label: Verse 91
units.deva:
तत्त्वज्ञानोदयादूर्ध्वं प्रारब्धं नैव विद्यते।
देहादीनामसत्यत्वाद्यथा स्वप्नः प्रबोधतः।।91।।
units.translation: Once truth is known, no prārabdha remains, as a dream vanishes upon waking, the body and such being unreal.

gloss.en: from the rise of true knowledge

units.label: Verse 92
units.deva:
कर्म जन्मान्तरकृतं प्रारब्धमिति कीर्तितम्।
तत्तु जन्मान्तराभावात्पुंसो नैवास्ति कर्हिचित्।।92।।
units.translation: Prārabdha is action done in a former birth; for one who has no further birth it cannot exist.

units.label: Verse 93
units.deva:
स्वप्नदेहो यथाध्यस्तस्तथैवायं हि देहकः।।
अध्यस्तस्य कुतो जन्म जन्माभावे स्थितिः कुतः।।93।।
units.translation: This body is superimposed like a dream-body. What birth can an imposed appearance have, and where is continuity without birth?

units.label: Verse 94
units.deva:
उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य मृद्भाण्डस्येव कथ्यते।
अज्ञानं चैव वेदान्तैस्तस्मिन्नष्टे क्व विश्वता।।94।।
units.translation: Vedānta says ignorance is the world's material cause, as earth is a pot's; when ignorance ends, where can the world remain?

units.label: Verse 95
units.deva:
यथा रज्जुं परित्यज्य सर्प गृह्णाति वै भ्रमात्।
तद्वत्सत्यमविज्ञाय जगत्पश्यति मूढधीः।।95।।
units.translation: As a confused person sees only a snake, not the rope, the fool sees the world without knowing the Real.

units.label: Verse 96
units.deva:
रज्जुरूपे परिज्ञाते सर्पभ्रान्तिर्न तिष्ठति।
अधिष्ठाने तथा ज्ञाते प्रपञ्चः शून्यतां व्रजेत्।।96।।
units.translation: Knowing the rope ends the snake-illusion; knowing the ground of being makes the phenomenal world vanish.

units.label: Verse 97
units.deva:
देहस्यापि प्रपञ्चत्वात्प्रारब्धावस्थितिः कुतः।
अज्ञानिजनबोधार्थं प्रारब्धं वक्ति वै श्रुतिः।।97।।
units.translation: Since the body itself belongs to the unreal world, how could prārabdha persist? Scripture speaks of it to instruct the ignorant.

units.label: Verse 98
units.deva:
क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे।
बहुत्वं तन्निषेधार्थं श्रुत्या गीतं च वै स्फुटम्।।98।।
units.translation: When the higher and lower are seen, actions perish; scripture's plural wording likewise denies any remaining prārabdha.

units.label: Verse 99
units.deva:
उच्यतेऽज्ञैर्बलाच्चैतत्तदानर्थद्वयागमः।
वेदान्तमतहानं च यतो ज्ञानमिति श्रुतिः।।99।।
units.translation: If the ignorant insist on it, they face contradictions and abandon Vedānta's conclusion; accept scripture that leads to knowledge.

units.label: Verse 100
units.deva:
त्रिपञ्चाङ्गान्यथो वक्ष्ये पूर्वोक्तस्यैव सिद्धये।
तैश्च सर्वैः सदा कार्यं निदिध्यासनमेव तु।।100।।
units.translation: I shall now explain fifteen limbs for the realization just taught; through all of them practice contemplation.

units.label: Verse 101
units.deva:
नित्याभ्यासादृते प्राप्तिर्न भवेत्सच्चिदात्मनः।
तस्माद्ब्रह्म निदिध्यासेज्जिज्ञासुः श्रेयसे चिरम्।।101।।
units.translation: The Self of Being-Consciousness is reached by steady practice; a seeker should meditate on Brahman for the highest good.

units.label: Verse 102
units.deva:
यमो हि नियमस्त्यागो मौनं देशश्च कालतः।
आसनं मूलबन्धश्च देहसाम्यं च दृक्स्थितिः।।102।।
units.translation: Yama, niyama, renunciation, silence, place, time, posture, root-lock, bodily balance, steady gaze—these are the first limbs.

units.label: Verse 103
units.deva:
प्राणसंयमनं चैव प्रत्याहारश्च धारणा।
आत्मध्यानं समाधिश्च प्रोक्तान्यङ्गानि वै क्रमात्।।103।।
units.translation: The remaining limbs, in order, are breath restraint, withdrawal, concentration, Self-meditation, and absorption.

units.label: Verse 104
units.deva:
सर्वं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानादिन्द्रियग्रामसंयमः।
यमोऽयमिति संप्रोक्तोऽभ्यसनीयो मुहुर्मुहुः।।104।।
units.translation: Restraint of the senses through the knowledge 'All this is Brahman' is yama, to be practiced repeatedly.

units.label: Verse 105
units.deva:
सजातीयप्रवाहश्च विजातीयतिरस्कृतिः।
नियमो हि परानन्दो नियमात्क्रियते बुधैः।।105।।
units.translation: Niyama is an unbroken flow of like thoughts that excludes unlike ones; the wise practice this supreme bliss.

units.label: Verse 106
units.deva:
त्यागः प्रपञ्चरूपस्य चिदात्मत्वावलोकनात्।
त्यागो हि महतां पूज्यः सद्यो मोक्षमयो यतः।।106।।
units.translation: Seeing the world as consciousness-Self is renunciation, honored by the great and identical with immediate liberation.

units.label: Verse 107
units.deva:
यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह।
यन्मौनं योगिभिर्गम्यं तद्भजेत्सर्वदा बुधः।।107।।
units.translation: The wise should always enter that silence beyond mind and speech, which yogins reach.

units.label: Verse 108
units.deva:
वाचो यस्मान्निवर्तन्ते तद्वक्तुं केन शक्यते।
प्रपञ्चो यदि वक्तव्यः सोऽपि शब्दविवर्जितः।।108।।
units.translation: Who can speak of that from which words return? Even the world, if described, eludes speech.

units.label: Verse 109
units.deva:
इति वा तद्भवेन्मौनं सतां सहजसंज्ञितम्।
गिरा मौनं तु बालानां प्रयुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिभिः।।109।।
units.translation: This is the natural silence known to the wise; merely restraining speech is the silence taught for the unknowing.

units.label: Verse 110
units.deva:
आदावन्ते च मध्ये च जनो यस्मिन्न विद्यते।
येनेदं सततं व्याप्तं स देशो विजनः स्मृतः।।110।।
units.translation: The solitary space is that in which no world of beings appears at any time, yet which pervades all this constantly.

units.label: Verse 111
units.deva:
कलनात्सर्वभूतानां ब्रह्मादीनां निमेषतः।
कालशब्देन निर्दिष्टो ह्यखण्डानन्द अद्वयः।।111।।
units.translation: The word 'time' denotes nondual, indivisible bliss, which brings all beings, from Brahmā onward, into existence in a moment.

gloss.en: in the twinkling of an eye

units.label: Verse 112
units.deva:
सुखेनैव भवेद्यस्मिन्नजस्रं ब्रह्मचिन्तनम्।
आसनं तद्विजानीयान्नेतरत्सुखनाशनम्।।112।।
units.translation: Know as posture the ease in which thought of Brahman flows uninterrupted; other postures destroy comfort.

units.label: Verse 113
units.deva:
सिद्धं यत्सर्वभूतादि विश्वाधिष्ठानमव्ययम्।
यस्मिन्सिद्धाः समाविष्टास्तद्वै सिद्धासनं विदुः।।113।।
units.translation: The immutable ground and origin of all, in which the perfected are absorbed, is called Siddhāsana.

units.label: Verse 114
units.deva:
यन्मूलं सर्वभूतानां यन्मूलं चित्तबन्धनम्।
मूलबन्धः सदा सेव्यो योगोऽसौ राजयोगिनाम्।।114।।
units.translation: The root from which all beings arise and on which mind-restraint depends is mūlabandha, the yogin's root-lock.

units.label: Verse 115
units.deva:
अङ्गानां समतां विद्यात्समे ब्रह्मणि लीयते।
नो चेन्नैव समानत्वमृजुत्वं शुष्कवृक्षवत्।।115।।
units.translation: True bodily balance is absorption in the uniform Brahman; standing straight like a dry tree is no equipoise.

units.label: Verse 116
units.deva:
दृष्टिं ज्ञानमयीं कृत्वा पश्येद्ब्रह्ममयं जगत्।
सा दृष्टिः परमोदारा न नासाग्रावलोकनी।।116।।
units.translation: Make vision knowledge-filled and see the world as Brahman; this noble seeing is not merely gazing at the nose-tip.

gloss.en: directed to the tip of the nose

units.label: Verse 117
units.deva:
द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यानां विरामो यत्र वा भवेत्।
दृष्टिस्तत्रैव कर्तव्या न नासाग्रावलोकनी।।117।।
units.translation: Fix sight where the distinction among seer, seeing, and seen ceases, not on the tip of the nose.

gloss.en: to the tip of the nose

units.label: Verse 118
units.deva:
चित्तादिसर्वभावेषु ब्रह्मत्वेनैव भावनात्।
निरोधः सर्ववृत्तीनां प्राणायामः स उच्यते।।118।।
units.translation: Restraining all thought by viewing every state of mind as Brahman is called prāṇāyāma.

units.label: Verse 119
units.deva:
निषेधनं प्रपञ्चस्य रेचकाख्यः समीरणः।
ब्रह्मैवास्मीति या वृत्तिः पूरको वायुरीरितः।।119।।
units.translation: Rechaka is negating the world; pūraka is the thought 'I am Brahman.'

units.label: Verse 120
units.deva:
ततस्तद्वृत्तिनैश्चल्यं कुम्भकः प्राणसंयमः।
अयं चापि प्रबुद्धानामज्ञानां घ्राणपीडनम्।।120।।
units.translation: Kumbhaka is the stillness of that thought: true breath restraint for the awakened; the ignorant merely torment the nose.

units.label: Verse 121
units.deva:
विषयेष्वात्मतां दृष्ट्वा मनसश्चिति मज्जनम्।
प्रत्याहारः स विज्ञेयोऽभ्यसनीयो मुमुक्षुभिः।।121।।
units.translation: Seeing the Self in every object, the mind merges into consciousness; seekers of liberation should practice this withdrawal.

units.label: Verse 122
units.deva:
यत्र यत्र मनो याति ब्रह्मणस्तत्र दर्शनात्।
मनसो धारणायैव धारणा सा परा मता।।122।।
units.translation: Wherever the mind goes, see Brahman there; steadiness grounded in that vision is supreme dhāraṇā.

units.label: Verse 123
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैवास्मीति सद्वृत्त्या निरालम्बतया स्थितिः।
ध्यानशब्देन विख्याता परमानन्ददायिनी।।123।।
units.translation: To remain unsupported in the clear thought “I am Brahman” is meditation, giver of supreme bliss.

units.label: Verse 124
units.deva:
निर्विकारतया वृत्त्या ब्रह्माकारतया पुनः।
वृत्तिविस्मरणं सम्यक्समाधिर्ज्ञानसंज्ञकः।।124।।
units.translation: Making thought changeless and shaped as Brahman, its complete subsidence is samādhi, known as knowledge.

units.label: Verse 125
units.deva:
एवं चाकृत्रिमानन्दं तावत्साधु समभ्यसेत्।
वश्यो यावत्क्षणात्पुंसः प्रयुक्तः स भेवत्स्वयम्।।125।।
units.translation: Practice this natural bliss until, mastered, it arises spontaneously at a moment's call.

units.label: Verse 126
units.deva:
ततः साधननिर्मुक्तः सिद्धो भवति योगिराट्।
तत्स्वरूपं न चैकस्य विषयो मनसो गिराम्।।126।।
units.translation: Then the perfected king of yogins is released from practices; that true nature is no object of mind or speech.

units.label: Verse 127
units.deva:
समाधौ क्रियमाणे तु विघ्ना आयान्ति वै बलात्।
अनुसंधानराहित्यमालस्यं भोगलालसम्।।127।।
units.translation: In samādhi, obstacles arise forcefully: lack of inquiry, idleness, and craving for pleasure.

units.label: Verse 128
units.deva:
लयस्तमश्च विक्षेपो रसास्वादश्च शून्यता।
एवं यद्विघ्नबाहुल्यं त्याज्यं ब्रह्मविदा शनैः।।128।।
units.translation: Sleep, dullness, distraction, savoring bliss, and emptiness are further obstacles; the knower should gradually abandon this multitude.

units.label: Verse 129
units.deva:
भाववृत्त्या हि भावत्वं शून्यवृत्त्या हि शून्यता।
ब्रह्मवृत्त्या हि पूर्णत्वं तथा पूर्णत्वमभ्यसेत्।।129।।
units.translation: The mind takes the form of an object when thinking of it and becomes void when thinking of emptiness; by Brahman-thought it becomes full—practice that fullness.

units.label: Verse 130
units.deva:
ये हि वृत्तिं जहत्येनां ब्रह्माख्यां पावनीं पराम्।
वृथैव ते तु जीवन्ति पशुभिश्च समा नराः।।130।।
units.translation: Those who abandon this pure, supreme thought of Brahman live in vain, no better than animals.

units.label: Verse 131
units.deva:
ये हि वृत्तिं विजानन्ति ये ज्ञात्वा वर्धयन्त्यपि।
ते वै सत्पुरुषा धन्या वन्द्यास्ते भुवनत्रये।।131।।
units.translation: Blessed and worthy of reverence in all worlds are those who know this thought and deepen it after knowing.

units.label: Verse 132
units.deva:
येषां वृत्तिः समावृद्धा परिपक्वा च सा पुनः।
ते वै सद्ब्रह्मतां प्राप्ता नेतरे शब्दवादिनः।।132।।
units.translation: Those whose awareness has grown and ripened attain the true state of Brahman; word-dealers do not.

units.label: Verse 133
units.deva:
कुशला ब्रह्मवार्तायां वृत्तिहीनाः सुरागिणः।
तेऽप्यज्ञानितमा नूनं पुनरायान्ति यान्ति च।।133।।
units.translation: Skilled in talking about Brahman yet without realization and attached to pleasures, the ignorant are born and die again.

units.label: Verse 134
units.deva:
निमेषार्धं न तिष्ठन्ति वृत्तिं ब्रह्ममयीं विना।
यथा तिष्ठन्ति ब्रह्माद्याः सनकाद्याः शुकादयः।।134।।
units.translation: Do not pass even half a moment without Brahman-awareness, as do Brahmā, Sanaka, Śuka, and the others.

units.label: Verse 135
units.deva:
कार्ये कारणतायाता कारणे न हि कार्यता।
कारणत्वं स्वतो गच्छेत्कार्याभावे विचारतः।।135।।
units.translation: The effect bears the nature of its cause, not the reverse; inquiry finds that without the effect, causehood itself falls away.

units.label: Verse 136
units.deva:
अथ शुद्धं भवेद्वस्तु यद्वै वाचामगोचरः।
द्रष्टव्यं मृद्धटेनैव दृष्टान्तेन पुनः पुनः।।136।।
units.translation: Then the pure reality beyond speech alone remains; understand it again and again through the example of clay and pot.

units.label: Verse 137
units.deva:
अनेनैव प्रकारेण वृत्तिर्ब्रह्मात्मिका भवेत्।
उदेति शुद्धचित्तानां वृत्तिज्ञानं ततः परम्।।137।।
units.translation: In this way a Brahman-shaped thought arises in the pure-minded; from it, knowledge dawns and merges into the beyond.

units.label: Verse 138
units.deva:
कारणं व्यतिरेकेण पुमानादौ विलोकयेत्।
अन्वयेन पुनस्तद्धि कार्ये नित्यं प्रपश्यति।।138।।
units.translation: First discern the cause by difference; then, through continuity, see it always present within the effect.

units.label: Verse 139
units.deva:
कार्ये हि कारणं पश्येत्पश्चात्कार्यं विसर्जयेत्।
कारणत्वं स्वतो नश्येदवशिष्टं भवेन्मुनिः।।139।।
units.translation: See the cause in the effect, then dismiss the effect; when causality falls away, the sage alone remains.

units.label: Verse 140
units.deva:
भावितं तीव्रवेगेण वस्तु यन्निश्चयात्मना।
पुमांस्तद्धि भवेच्छीघ्रं ज्ञेयं भ्रमरकीटवत्।।140।।
units.translation: Whatever a person contemplates intensely and with conviction, they soon become, as the wasp and worm illustrate.

gloss.en: like the wasp and the worm

units.label: Verse 141
units.deva:
अदृश्यं भावरूपं च सर्वमेतच्चिदात्मकम्।
सावधानतया नित्यं स्वात्मानं भावयेद्बुधः।।141।।
units.translation: The wise should carefully and constantly regard all things, visible and invisible, as the Self that is consciousness.

units.label: Verse 142
units.deva:
दृश्यं ह्यदृश्यतां नीत्वा ब्रह्माकारेण चिन्तयेत्।
विद्वान्नित्यसुखे तिष्ठेद्धिया चिद्रसपूर्णया।।142।।
units.translation: Having withdrawn the seen into the unseen, contemplate all as Brahman; the knower abides in lasting joy, mind full of conscious bliss.

units.label: Verse 143
units.deva:
एभिरङ्गैः समायुक्तो राजयोग उदाहृतः।
किंचित्पक्वकषायाणां हठयोगेन संयुतः।।143।।
units.translation: These limbs together are called rāja-yoga; haṭha-yoga accompanies it for those whose residual desires are partly weakened.

units.label: Verse 144
units.deva:
परिपक्वं मनो येषां केवलोऽयं च सिद्धिदः।
गुरुदैवतभक्तानां सर्वेषां सुलभो जवात्।।144।।
units.translation: For minds made mature, this alone swiftly grants perfection; devotion to teacher and deity makes it readily accessible.

gloss.en: of those devoted to teacher and deity

units.label: Closing colophon
units.deva:
इति श्रीमत्परमहंसपरिव्राजकाचार्यस्य
श्रीगोविन्दभगवत्पूज्यपादशिष्यस्य
श्रीमच्छंकरभगवतः कृतौ
अपरोक्षानुभूतिः समाप्ता।।
units.translation: Thus ends the Aparokṣānubhūti, composed by the revered Śaṅkara, disciple of the venerable Govindapāda, as a supreme ascetic and wandering teacher.
